evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/price_data.py:39 (range_ default '6mo'), sidecar/services/agent_tools/price_data.py:59 (recent_bars = list(series.bars)[-90:]), sidecar/services/agent_tools/price_data.py:60-79 (response carries symbol/timeframe/provider but no bar counts)
notes: Same class as the analyst/earnings row caps (analyst_tools.py:29 _MAX_HISTORY_ROWS=60, earnings_tools.py:75 [:12]) where 'count' reports the CAPPED length, so the model cannot tell a truncation from a short history. The truncation itself is correct (prompt budget); the silence is the defect. Smallest fix: return bars_returned + bars_available (and window_start) alongside bars, and say so in the catalog.py tool description so the model narrows its claim instead of over-claiming.

refuter.reason: Confirmed: range defaults to '6mo' and the handler returns list(series.bars)[-90:] with no bars_available/window marker, and the catalog description (catalog.py:147-159) advertises range 'e.g. 1mo, 6mo, 1y' without mentioning the cap — so range=1y also yields ~4.3 months of daily bars. Partial mitigation: each bar carries its timestamp, so the true window is derivable, but nothing tells the model to check.

title: Earnings, Analyst-Ratings and SEC panels are dead ends: they publish no panel context and consume no symbol command bus
repro: Open the Earnings Calendar (or Analyst Ratings, or SEC Filings) and ask the chat agent what is on screen — the panel contributes nothing to the preamble. Click a symbol in an earnings row, or a symbol chip on a news item: nothing happens; neither opens the chart or the equity overview.
evidence: src/modules/earnings/EarningsCalendarPanel.tsx:347, src/modules/news/NewsFeedPanel.tsx:136-143, src/modules/news/NewsFeedPanel.tsx:187-207, src/modules/equity-overview/EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:620-661, src/store/equity-command.ts:1-33, src/modules/chat/context-provider.ts
notes: Verified by grep: `usePanelContextBus` publishers are watchlist / chart / news / portfolio / equity-overview / backtest / chat only; there are ZERO references to panel-context, equity-command or chart-command anywhere under src/modules/earnings, src/modules/analyst-ratings, src/modules/sec. Two consequences in an agent-first product: (a) the agent cannot see three of the app's data panels, though context-provider.ts builds its preamble from exactly that bus; (b) every symbol those panels render is inert — an earnings row's symbol, a news item's symbol chips (plain <span>s), an insider reporter — while CLAUDE.md documents the brief's ticker chips doing exactly this via the always-consumed chart-command seam. Smallest fix: one publishPanelContext effect per panel (copy NewsFeedPanel.tsx:187-207) and make the symbol cell a button calling useEquityCommandStore.getState().loadSymbol.

refuter.reason: Both halves hold: no file under src/modules/earnings, analyst-ratings or sec references the panel-context bus or the equity/chart command stores, and news symbol chips are plain <span>s (NewsFeedPanel.tsx:136-143). The mechanism and fix are understated, though. The agent's snapshot builder (context-provider.ts captureTerminalState) only reads chart*, watchlist and portfolio sources from the bus and drops every other source, including news and equity, which already publish. So copying NewsFeedPanel's publish effect would still leave these panels invisible to the agent; captureTerminalState must also be taught the new sources. The agent does see these panels' ids via openPanels (:280-292), but not their contents.

title: Three of the eight hand-written MCP tools turn an unreachable router into an empty list, so an external LLM is told 'no agents / no workflows / no runs' instead of 'broken'
repro: design + code path. mcp_server.py:168-180 list_agents catches httpx.HTTPError and returns {'agents': []}; :297-313 list_workflows and :350-364 list_runs do the same. The same branch is reachable from _internal_client's own unbound fallback at :94 (base_url='http://127.0.0.1:0'), whose comment claims it 'exists so an early failure produces a useful error'. Meanwhile :244, :252 and :334 call raise_for_status() bare so a 404 escapes the tool as a raw httpx error.
evidence: sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:178, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:311, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:362, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:94, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:244, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:252, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:334, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:120
notes: Consistency + swallowed exception becomes a silent empty: one file ships three incompatible error policies (swallow-to-empty, let-it-escape, return-{ok:false} at :116-122), so the next tool author has no rule and an MCP client sees three failure shapes. Consequence: this is the product's external agent-native face - Claude Desktop asking Vysted 'what agents do you have?' while the agents router is unreachable receives a confident 'none', indistinguishable from a build with no agents; the same for saved workflows and in-flight Delegate runs (a user could conclude a durable run vanished). Smallest fix: one policy for the file - return {'<key>': [], 'error': '<reason>'} so empty is distinguishable from broken, wrap the three bare raise_for_status() sites in it, and delete the 127.0.0.1:0 fallback at :94 (it cannot produce a useful error while three of its four consumers eat it).

refuter.reason: The swallow-to-empty is real (list_agents/list_workflows/list_runs map any httpx.HTTPError to an empty list), but the trigger is mis-stated: in production bind_app is always called so the tools use the in-process ASGITransport and the 127.0.0.1:0 fallback is unreachable; the actual path is a 5xx from the in-process route -> raise_for_status HTTPStatusError (an HTTPError) -> confident empty list. The three bare raise_for_status sites do not escape as raw transport errors either - FastMCP/lowlevel server convert a raising tool into an isError=True result. A rare in-process 5xx is a medium, not high, silent degradation.

repro: A plugin AgentSpec whose `tools` contains an id outside the sidecar allow-list: POST /custom-agents returns 4xx, the response is never inspected, the catch only covers network errors -> the Marketplace reports the plugin Enabled and the agent never appears in the roster, with nothing logged.

Becomes live the moment a plugin ships a tool id the catalog does not project. Fix: check response.ok, treat 409 as success explicitly, and surface anything else through the runtime's `errored` event so the Plugin Manager shows it.

title: Research LLM calls are structurally unmeterable: token and spend ceilings can never fire and brief cost always reports zero
repro: Run any native research brief. LLMCall is typed Callable[[list[dict]], Awaitable[str]] (deep.py:54) - there is no channel for usage - so every budget call site passes None: citecheck.py:266, deep.py:1214, iter.py:585, iter.py:962, iter.py:1023, verify.py:319. BudgetGuard.record returns immediately after ticking _steps when usage is None (budget_guard.py:126-127), so _tokens and _spend_usd stay 0 for the whole run. breach() checks tokens then spend first (budget_guard.py:152-158) and neither can ever trip. BudgetGuard.cost() therefore returns {'tokens': 0, 'spend_usd': 0.0, 'steps': n} -> ResearchBrief.cost (models.py:168) -> formatBriefTokens(0) and formatBriefSpend(0) both return null (brief-ingest.ts:445, brief-ingest.ts:459) -> the cockpit shows NO cost for a native deep run while the Sonar lane shows '~$0.25 (estimate)' (sonar.py:224-238).
evidence: sidecar/services/research/deep.py:54, sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:126, sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:152, sidecar/services/research/citecheck.py:266, sidecar/services/research/iter.py:1023, sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:232, sidecar/services/research/models.py:168, src/lib/brief-ingest.ts:445
notes: A ceiling with no meter. Two of the four SC-008 ceilings named in CLAUDE.md are dead code on the research path - only steps and wall-clock bound a run, so an expensive model cannot be stopped by cost. Second consequence is a data-trust one: a zero that means UNMEASURED renders as ABSENCE, so a user comparing the native lane against the paid Sonar lane concludes the native lane is free. models.py:155 documents cost as 'the BudgetGuard.cost snapshot' without saying it is always zero. Smallest fix: widen LLMCall to return (str, LLMUsage | None) and thread the real usage into the six existing record() call sites - the receiving plumbing already exists. Interim: state 'not metered' in the contract and the cockpit rather than rendering nothing.

refuter.reason: Real. The research llm_call wraps oneshot.complete, which returns only a str (deep_research.py:322-325, oneshot.py:46-53), so every research record() call passes None and cost() reports tokens 0 / spend 0.0, which the cockpit then omits. Mechanism correction: the research BudgetGuard is built with only max_steps and max_wall_seconds (deep_research.py:232-235), so its token and spend ceilings are never set at all. The more serious consequence is that research-internal LLM spend never reaches ANY guard, including a durable delegate run's own spend ceiling.

title: News sentiment scoring and symbol tagging live in the HTTP route, so the agent and MCP surface receive unscored, untagged news while the docstring claims parity
repro: Call the `news` agent tool. news_tool.py:46 calls news_provider.fetch_news directly and returns item.model_dump() at news_tool.py:55 with no enrichment; every NewsItem therefore carries sentiment=None, sentiment_label=None, symbols=[] (defaults at models/news.py:24-26). The GET /news route does the enrichment itself at news.py:115-130 (sentiment.score_text + _tag_symbols). Second half: _tag_symbols' regex (news.py:72) is \b-anchored and needs the literal symbol string, so a raw watchlist symbol like 'BTC/USDT' never matches a headline saying 'Bitcoin'/'BTC'; because `requested` is non-empty the route then drops every untagged item (news.py:120-121) and returns an empty list. The frontend defends this by projecting through toNewsSymbol (NewsFeedPanel.tsx:170, BTC/USDT -> BTC); the agent path has no such projection.
evidence: sidecar/routers/news.py:115, sidecar/routers/news.py:72, sidecar/routers/news.py:120, sidecar/services/agent_tools/news_tool.py:4, sidecar/services/agent_tools/news_tool.py:46, sidecar/models/news.py:24, src/modules/news/NewsFeedPanel.tsx:170
notes: Different-layer-different-abstraction violation plus a failure to pull complexity downward: the route owns enrichment that belongs to the service, so the second consumer of the same data silently degrades. news_tool.py:4-5 states 'Mirrors what GET /news serves' - it does not, and the finance-tuned agent (the product) is structurally blind to the sentiment the panel displays. The blindness is quiet: sentiment exists and is null, which reads as neutral/unknown rather than never-computed. The symbol invariant likewise lives in one frontend helper instead of at the boundary. Smallest fix: move scoring + tagging + symbol normalisation into news_provider.fetch_news (or a shared news_provider.enrich()); the route becomes a thin projection and the agent-tool docstring becomes true.

refuter.reason: Holds. The agent `news` tool returns fetch_news items raw (news_tool.py:46-55), and fetch_news builds items with symbols=[] and no sentiment (news_provider.py:213, :255). Only the GET /news route scores and tags them (news.py:115-130), which contradicts the tool docstring's 'Mirrors what GET /news serves'. The raw-symbol half is also live: GET /news?symbols=BTC/USDT returns [] while symbols=BTC returns 6 items. Scope nuance: the agent tool does not filter by tag, so the agent gets unfiltered, unscored news rather than an empty list. The empty-list trap bites only raw-symbol callers of the route.

title: Two agent tools run the 300-900 ms (worst case 30 s) resolver on the event loop while both routers asyncio.to_thread it
repro: Any agent 'research <name>' call: agent_tools/__init__.py:67 awaits the handler on the loop; agent_tools/resolve_symbol.py:70 calls the synchronous symbol_resolver.resolve directly. Measured masters-only cost (sidecar/.venv/bin/python, _live_lookup stubbed): 'infosys' 313 ms, 'tata steel' 653 ms, 'reliance q4 results' 783 ms, 'hdfc bank limited results' 897 ms. A master miss falls through to yf.Search (yfinance 1.3.0 defaults timeout=30, raise_errors=True; no explicit timeout passed), so the loop can stall 30 s.
evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/resolve_symbol.py:70, sidecar/services/agent_tools/fundamentals.py:119, sidecar/services/agent_tools/__init__.py:67, sidecar/routers/resolve.py:93, sidecar/routers/fundamentals.py:73, sidecar/routers/resolve.py:70, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:1001
notes: Pull complexity downward / consistency: the sibling routers offload and DOCUMENT why ('must not block the event loop', routers/resolve.py:70-72), and symbol_resolver.py:658-660 cites the router's to_thread call as load-bearing for the signature -- so the author knew. The hottest resolver path in the product is the one that opted out. Consequence: every agent name-resolve stalls the whole sidecar (SSE streams, /health, the detached run manager) for ~0.6 s, or 30 s on a hung upstream. Smallest fix: 'await asyncio.to_thread(symbol_resolver.resolve, query, region)' in both tools, plus an explicit timeout= on yf.Search.

refuter.reason: Holds: resolve_symbol awaits nothing and calls the synchronous resolver on the event loop, the dispatcher just awaits the handler, and yfinance 1.3.0's Search defaults to timeout=30 with no override passed, while both routers offload to a thread. Correction to scope: fundamentals.py reaches _canonicalize only on the failure fallback after the fetch retries, not on every call, and measured master-only stalls on this machine were ~150-380 ms rather than 313-897 ms; the 30 s worst case (master miss plus hung upstream) still stands, after which the 60 s cooldown damps repeats.

repro: Launch with provider=openrouter + key, let it breach (status=error), POST /runs/{id}/resume -> invoke_agent is called with provider/model/api_key all None (proved: scratch script prints `P4 resume invoke kwargs: {'provider': None, 'model': None, 'api_key': None}`), so it falls to spec.default_provider ('anthropic' for 10 bundled agents, keyless -> error; 'ollama' -> cold-loads a local model).
evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:401-412 (hard-coded None), sidecar/routers/runs.py:118 and :130 (routes never pass api_key/budget although the manager accepts them - test-only parameters, see sidecar/tests/test_run_manager.py:270,293), sidecar/models/run.py:144-149 (answer body has no key field), sidecar/services/runs_store.py:75 (allow-list persists only research_depth/region), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:524-536 (None -> agent defaults), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:399 (resume zeroes the recorded cost, so lifetime spend across resumes is understated), src/lib/delegate-runs.ts:226 (resumeDelegateRun has zero callers)

Severity lowered high->medium because no UI path reaches either resume (resumeDelegateRun has zero callers) or answer (no pause trigger, finding 10), so no user hits the failure today - it is a dead/false SC-008 claim rather than a broken core flow.

title: Spend ceiling can overshoot: a breach flagged at a round boundary cannot stop the loop, so that round's tools run and the next provider request is sent (and never metered)
repro: Faked provider that emits tool_use + done(100k tokens) every round, RunBudget(max_tokens=1000): the run aborts with 'token ceiling' but the provider was called TWICE (scratch proof prints `P5 ... provider calls after 1-round breach: 2 | cost: tokens=100000`) - round 2's request went out after the breach and its usage is not in the recorded cost.
evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:133-140 (callback only sets a flag), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:176-178 (the consumer can act only on the NEXT yielded event), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1466-1473 (callback fires, then `break` to tool dispatch), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1551-1575 (all pending tools dispatched - incl. paid search / deep research - before any event is guaranteed), sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:1-8 ('hard spend ceiling', 'aborts 100%')
notes: Pull complexity downward: the stop decision lives in the consumer although the only point synchronous with the round boundary is the callback. Consequence: a '$1 hard ceiling' lets one extra tool batch plus one extra provider request through, and the rail under-reports what was spent. Fix shape: let the callback stop the loop - raise a private _BudgetBreach(reason) from _on_round_usage and catch it in _drive_run (or have on_round_usage return a stop bool that invoke_agent honours before dispatching tools).

title: A run that completes on the round that touches a ceiling is recorded as `error`
repro: One-shot provider (delta + done), RunBudget(max_steps=1) -> row is status=error, detail='step ceiling 1 reached (1 taken)' while its transcript holds the complete answer (scratch proof P2). Same for a final round that crosses max_tokens / max_spend_usd.

title: Resume and answer corrupt the conversation: the original prompt is replayed as the NEWEST turn after the human's answer, and a second answer turns the first answer into the prompt
repro: launch('ORIGINAL PROMPT') -> pause -> answer('ANSWER ONE'): provider receives [assistant, user 'ANSWER ONE', user 'ORIGINAL PROMPT']. pause -> answer('ANSWER TWO'): provider receives [..., user 'ORIGINAL PROMPT', assistant, user 'ANSWER TWO', user 'ANSWER ONE'] - the prompt is now the first answer (scratch proof P1a/P1b).
evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:126-129 (_drive_run writes history first, then the prompt, so the checkpoint no longer starts with the prompt), :369-382 (resume assumes 'first user turn = prompt'), :338-343 (answer appended as a raw dict), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:518-520 (history, then prompt as the last message), sidecar/services/run_manager.py:164-173 (tool RESULTS are never checkpointed, so a resumed run re-pays every tool call), sidecar/services/runs_store.py:27-28 (column documented as 'the accumulated messages list' - it is a display digest)
notes: Information leakage: the checkpoint format is known to four places (_drive_run, answer_run, resume_run, _digest_transcript) and its one invariant is broken by its own writer. Reachable today only via the API (see finding 10), hence medium. Fix shape: store {prompt, turns[]} explicitly (prompt as its own field) and on answer send the ANSWER as the new prompt with the prior turns as history.

title: Gemini thought signatures are dropped on multi-round tool turns: the adapter keeps only name/args and rebuilds function_call parts without the signature Google documents as required for function calling on Gemini 3
repro: design (code read) + NOT TESTED live. GeminiProvider.stream_chat reads only fc.name / fc.id / fc.args from each part (the Part's thought_signature field, present in google-genai 2.5.0, `'thought_signature' in types.Part.model_fields` -> True, is never read). LLMToolUseEvent has no slot to carry it. _split_system_and_contents rebuilds the model turn as {'function_call': {name, args}} parts. Round 2 of any Gemini 3 tool turn therefore replays function calls without their signatures. Live confirmation needs a Gemini key (none funded on this run's lanes). Cost: one 2-round agent invoke on a Gemini 3 Flash-class model, < $0.01.

We recommend you always pass all signatures back as received, but it's *required* for function calling signatures.'; line 649: 'Return the entire response with all parts back to the model in subsequent turns.'; line 651: 'Don't merge one part with a signature with another part without a signature.'); https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3.md.txt (line 226: 'If you are managing conversation history manually, you must include thought blocks with their signatures in subsequent requests to validate authenticity.')
notes: Principle: research P2 (echo reasoning state verbatim; rules differ by model). The runtime already solved the analogous DeepSeek-reasoner echo (agent_runtime.py:1527-1529) and the Gemini name-pairing trap (P1). The signature is the third member of that family and is missing. It compounds with COD-llm-adapters-2-3: Google documents the function+google_search round the runtime sends as valid only on Gemini 3, and Gemini 3 is exactly where dropping the signature is documented as required. On Gemini 2.5 (the default) the signature is returned with thinking plus function calling, and dropping it degrades reasoning continuity rather than being a documented hard failure. Smallest fix: add an optional `provider_meta: dict` to LLMToolUseEvent, capture part.thought_signature (bytes, base64 in transit) in gemini.py, carry it through metadata['tool_calls'][i], and re-attach it to the matching function_call part in _split_system_and_contents. Add a wire-shape replay test per WLD-harness-tools-2.

Google's docs (fetched copies) state signatures are required for function calling on Gemini 3. Not live-tested (no Gemini key), so the Gemini-3 hard failure is documented, not observed; on the 2.5 default it is a continuity degradation.
